newsitem.title: CHINA: China to restrict building of new ports.
newsitem.headline: China to restrict building of new ports.

text.p: China will restrict the building of new ports and will merge or close those port facilities that see too little traffic or are poorly managed, the China Daily said on Friday.
China has enough ports, but they are often hampered by poor layouts and chaotic management, it quoted Vice-Premier Zou Jiahua as telling a national conference on port administration.
"China plans to resolve the situation by regulating approval procedures for new ports and reorganising existing ports," Zou was quoted as saying.

The State Port Adminstration Office was surveying ports across the country and would recommend merging some small ports and closing those that have too little business, the newspaper quoted port office director Ye Jian as saying.
China's poorer central and western areas should not open ports illegally to seek faster economic growth, Ye warned.

"Ports should not be opened in areas where port operations are not eligible. Those areas should be encouraged to use existing ports in coastal and frontier areas," Ye said. China had 235 ports opened by the central government and 350 set up by provincial authorities, it said without elaborating.
